Staff Software Engineer 
Location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States

Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human
 Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.
This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.
 This role supports Okta's U.S. federal environments and requires U.S. federal eligibility, including U.S. citizenship. 
 The Team 
 Okta Workflows is a no-code automation platform that lets IT and security teams automate identity processes at scale: onboarding and offboarding, access requests, event-driven responses to security signals, and integrations across hundreds of SaaS applications. Every one of those automations ultimately runs on a single execution engine, and that is where this team lives. 
 The Opportunity 
 The Engine Kernel team owns the runtime that executes every Okta Workflow. Our engine treats a workflow the way an operating system treats a process: it schedules, pauses, resumes, and coordinates executions across a high-throughput, multi-region distributed system. The engine is written in Rust and runs on Kubernetes. 
 We are accountable for the reliability, scale, performance, and cost of the core workflow lifecycle, and we hold a very high bar for availability because our customers' identity automation depends on it. 
 Some of the problems you would work on: 
• Durable execution: evolving how the engine persists and recovers workflow state so long-running automations are resilient by design. 
• Smarter scheduling: reducing the cost of durability so the engine can checkpoint work cheaply and keep latency low and predictable. 
• Resilience under load: building adaptive throttling and backpressure directly into the runtime. 
• Efficiency at scale: cutting I/O, compute, and infrastructure cost as workflow volume grows, without giving up performance. 
• Operational excellence: improving observability, tooling, and automation so we find and fix issues before customers notice. 
 AI Assisted Engineering 
 We actively use AI coding assistants (such as Claude, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini) to move faster across the development lifecycle: prototyping, refactoring, generating tests, and documenting complex systems. We are looking for an engineer who uses these tools well and has the judgment to review, debug, and harden AI-generated code before it reaches a system that runs our customers' identity automation. 
 What you’ll be doing  
 As a Staff Software Engineer on the Engine Kernel team, you will: 
• Own large engine projects end to end, from design and spikes through implementation, rollout, monitoring, and alerting, and deliver them on time with a high bar for quality. 
• Design components of a high-throughput distributed runtime independently, bring them through design review, and make sound trade-offs between latency, durability, cost, and complexity. 
• Use proofs of concept, benchmarks, and production observability tools to make data-driven decisions about engine behavior and performance. 
• Participate in the team's Guardian and vulnerability triage rotations: independently troubleshoot production incidents, identify root causes, and drive remediation. 
• Drive operational improvement projects, such as reducing alert noise, closing monitoring gaps, and hardening the infrastructure the engine runs on. 
• Identify tech debt in a mature, evolving codebase, explain its impact on team velocity, and lead the work to pay it down. 
• Partner with adjacent Workflows teams (API, routing, data layer, connectors, infrastructure, SRE) and with Product to shape requirements for reliability, performance, and resilience. 
• Help customers have a great experience by working with Support, Customer Success, and the field on escalations that reach the engine. 
• Raise the bar for the team through thoughtful code reviews, mentoring, and sharing knowledge widely. 
 What you’ll bring to the role 
• U.S. citizenship and the ability to meet U.S. federal eligibility requirements for this role. 
• 6+ years of professional software engineering experience building and operating backend or distributed systems in production. 
• Strong proficiency in Rust , or deep experience in another systems language (C++) and a clear interest in becoming productive in Rust quickly. 
• Solid understanding of asynchronous and concurrent programming: event loops, async runtimes (for example, Tokio), thread pools, and the performance trade-offs between I/O-bound and CPU-bound work. 
• Hands-on experience with distributed systems building blocks such as message brokers (RabbitMQ, Kafka, or similar), in-memory data stores (Redis, or similar), and object storage, including failure modes like duplicate delivery, races, lock contention, and head-of-line blocking. 
• Experience running services on Kubernetes in a major cloud provider (AWS and/or GCP), with Docker and Linux and networking fundamentals. 
• A track record of owning production systems: designing for observability, writing meaningful alerts, participating in on-call, and leading incident root cause analysis. 
• Comfort jumping into large, unfamiliar codebases and quickly becoming productive. 
• Clear written and verbal communication: you share status, surface risks early, and can explain a design to both engineers and non-engineers. 
 And extra credit if you have experience in any of the following!  
• Experience building workflow engines, job schedulers, actor systems, or durable execution platforms (for example, Temporal, Cadence, or similar). 
• Experience with event sourcing, shared logs, optimistic concurrency control, or other techniques for building recoverable stateful systems. 
• Experience with cost optimization or multi-cloud deployments. 
• Familiarity with OpenTelemetry, Splunk, or other observability tooling at scale, and with defining and operating SLIs and SLOs. 
• Experience with Node.js / TypeScript services, or with migrating legacy systems to Rust. 
• Experience working on systems subject to FedRAMP or other regulated compliance environments. 
• Contributions to open source, conference talks, or technical writing. 
 Must attend in-person onboarding the first week of employment in Chicago, IL.
• Must go to office 2 days a week
